definitions.explanation: A common flying insect with two wings, often found around food and waste.

examples.japanese: {蠅|はえ}も{殺|ころ}さぬ{顔|かお}をしている。
examples.english: He has a face like he wouldn't hurt a fly. (Looks innocent)
examples.notes: Common expression for someone who looks harmless

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}になると{台所|だいどころ}に{蠅|はえ}が{集|あつ}まってくるので{困|こま}る。
examples.english: In summer, flies gather in the kitchen and it's a nuisance.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けたら{蠅|はえ}が{何匹|なんびき}も{入|はい}ってきたので、{蠅叩|はえたた}きで{退治|たいじ}した。
examples.english: When I opened the window, several flies came in, so I got rid of them with a fly swatter.

notes:
Also written as ハエ. Common species:
- イエバエ (housefly)
- キンバエ (blowfly)
- ショウジョウバエ (fruit fly)

Expressions:
- {蠅|はえ}も{殺|ころ}さぬ (wouldn't hurt a fly - looks innocent)
- {蠅叩|はえたた}き (fly swatter)
- {蠅取|はえと}り{紙|がみ} (fly paper)

Associated with:
- Unsanitary conditions
- Summer nuisance
- Quick, erratic movement

Related vocabulary:
- ブンブン (buzzing sound)
- {虫除|むしよ}け (insect repellent)
- {殺虫剤|さっちゅうざい} (insecticide)
- {蠅叩|はえたた}き (fly swatter)

The kanji {蠅|はえ} is complex; ハエ (katakana) is often used instead.

Counter: {一匹|いっぴき}, {二匹|にひき}...
